newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor gets 100 pct Mozambique licence firm.
newsitem.headline: Gencor gets 100 pct Mozambique licence firm.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor Ltd announced on Wednesday it had increased its stake in exploration licence holding company Genbique to 100 percent.
Genbique holds the exploration licences for economic minerals at Moebase and Quelimane in northern Mozambique -- areas with a large heavy minerals resource.
"Doctor Fred Roux, executive director of Gencor, announced today that Gencor has exercised an option to increase its shareholding in Genbique to 100 percent," Gencor said in a statement.
Last July, after the completion of a pre-feasibility study on the area, Gencor increased its holding in Genbique to 50 percent from 16.6 percent.
Gencor on Tuesday acquired the remaining 50 percent from Bermuda-based partners Edlow Resources Ltd.

The Moebase resource was proved to be one of the largest in the world after an intensive drilling programme of about 30,000 metres delineated a resource of 1.3 billion tonnes with an average grade of 3.8 percent heavy minerals, Gencor said.
At Quelimane a resource of 520 million tonnes at 4.5 percent heavy minerals was inferred.
A detailed feasibility study is in progress to determine the appropriate market entry in terms of timing and production volume.
The project will produce titanium slag, pig iron, rutile and zircon.
